**Steve Docherty (Stephen Docherty) - Died 1-1-2008 - Snowmobiling accident - He was 43 years old - Singer - Was a member of Power Ten.**

**Ben Marlin (aka Benny) - Died 1-2-2008 - Cancer ( Metal ) Born 3-18-1976 - Bassist - Was a member of Strangulation and [Disgorge](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disgorge).**

**Jimmy Ray (Ray A. Staszak) - Died 1-2-2008 - Colon cancer - Born 7-3-1910 in Bridgeport - Played clarinet and saxophone - Led The Jimmy Ray Orchestra.**

**O.G. Style (Eric Woods) (aka Prince Ezzy-E)- Died 1-3-2008 - Brain hemorrhage ( Rap ) He was 37 years old - (He did, "Catch 'Em Slippin' (I Know How To Play 'Em)" and "Steppin' on Toes") - Worked with K-Rino and Bun B.**

**Margie Gray (Margie Hoffman Toscano) - Died 1-3-2008 - Heart attack - She was 83 years old - Singer - Worked with Boyd Raeburn, Randy Brooks, Gray Adams and Bobby Sherwood.**

**Stanley Gaines Sr. - Died 1-3-2008 - Congestive heart failure - Born in Atlantic City - He was 80 years old - Guitarist - Led Stanley Gaines And The Hurricanes.**

**[Henri Chopin](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_Chopin) - Died 1-3-2008 ( Avant-garde ) Born 6-18-1922 in Paris, France - Sound poet and musician.**

**Winchester Davis - Died 1-4-2008 - He was 99 years old - Played saxophone - Led Little Wynn And The Deluxe Aces.**

**[Mort Garson](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mort_Garson) - Died 1-4-2008 in San Francisco, CA, U.S. - Renal failure ( Electronic ) Born 7-20-1924 in Saint John, New Brunswick, Canada - Composer, arranger and accompaniest - Played the Moog synthesizer - (He co-wrote Ruby And The Romantics', "Our Day Will Come") - Worked with Mel Torme, The Lettermen, The Sandpipers, The Sugar Shoppe, The Hollyrdige Strings, The Sunset Strings, Doris Day, Glenn Yarborough and Glen Campbell.**

**Doc Soul Stirrer (Harry Young, Jr.) - Died 1-4-2008 in Bessemer, Alabama. U.S. - Heart attack ( Rock - Blues ) Born 5-8-1940 in Baltimore, MD, U.S. - Singer and columnist.**

**Earl May (Earl Charles Barrington May) - Died 1-4-2008 in South Orange, NJ, U.S. - Heart attack - Born 9-17-1927 in Harlem, NY, U.S. - Bassist - Led The Earl May Quartet - Worked with Carmen McRae, Coleman Hawkins, Cab Calloway, Doc Cheatham, Ruth Brown, Jon Hendricks, Frank Foster, Dizzy Gillespie, Gloria Lynne, Moms Mabley, Charlie Parker, Miles Davis, Mercer Ellington, The Buddy Rich Big Band, John Coltrane, Herbie Mann and Lester Young.**

**Tony Ben (Anthony Joseph Ben) - Died 1-4-2008 ( Jazz - Disco ) Born 8-2-1942 - Drummer - Worked with The Sylvers, Ronnie Laws And Pressure and A Taste Of Honey ("Boogie Oogie Oogie") - CCHS Music Hall Of Fame Inductee.**

**Arcani Crosswords (Michael Francis) - Died 1-4-2008 - Accidental self inflicted gun shot ( Rap ) He was 32 years old - Co-owner of Fam Tide Records.**

**Irene Reid (Irene Frances Redfield) - Died 1-4-2008 in Bronx, NY - Cardiac arrest ( Jazz ) Born 9-23-1930 in Savannah, GA, U.S. - Singer - Led Irene Reid And Company - Worked with Charles Earland, The Dick Vance band and Count Basie's band - Appeared in Broadway's, "The Wiz".**

**[Vernon Derrick](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_Derrick) - Died 1-4-2008 ( Country ) Born 1933 in Grant, AL, U.S. - Played fiddle and mandolin - Worked with Hank Williams Jr., Flatt And Scruggs, The Stanley Brothers and Jimmy Martin And The Sunny Mountain Boys.**

**[Keith Baxter](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Baxter_%28drummer%29) - Died 1-4-2008 - Heart attack ( Rock ) Born 1971 in Lancaster, U.K - Drummer - Was a member of [Skyclad](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skyclad_%28band%29), [3 Colours Red](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3_Colours_Red), Elevation and Baby Judas.**

**Keith Smith (Keith John Smith) - Died 1-4-2008 in London, England ( Jazz ) Born 3-19-1940 in Isleworth, Middlesex - Trumpeter and bandleader - Worked with The San Jacinto Jazz Band, The New Teao Brass Band, Mickey Ashman, Mac Duncan, Bobby Mickleburgh's Confederates, The Climax Jazz Band, George Lewis, Papa Bue's Viking Jazz Band, Hefty Jazz, The Louis Armstrong All Stars and The Fron-Zi-Me Jazz Band.**

**Leigh Tomlinson - Died 1-5-2008 - Breast cancer ( Jazz ) Born 1961 in Fort Worth, TX, U.S. - Singer and actress - Led her own quartet and sang with The Sammons Jazz Program.**

**[Drew Glackin](http://www.drewglackin.com/index.html) (Andrew Glackin) - Died 1-5-2008 - Heart damage ( Country ) Born 1963 - Bassist - Was a member of Scapegoat and [The Silos](http://www.thesilos.net/) (They did, "Come On Like The Fast Lane" and "Sunset Morning") - Worked with Graham Parker, The Hold Steady and Susan Tedeschi.**

**[Ken Nelson](http://www.rockabillyhall.com/KenNelson1.html) (Kenneth F. Nelson)- Died 1-6-2008 in Somis, CA, U.S. - Born 1-19-1911 in Caledonia, Minn, U.S.- Was the head of country A&R for Capitol Records - Produced Hank Thompson, Buck Owens, Merle Haggard, Wanda Jackson, Ferlin Husky, Wynn Stewart, Tommy Collins, The Louvin Brothers a and Jean Shepard - [Country Music Hall Of Fame Inductee](http://www.countrymusichalloffame.com/site/inductees.aspx?cid=147).**

**Cy Leslie (Seymour Marvin Leslie) - Died 1-6-2008 in Roslyn, NY, U.S. - Born 12-16-1922 in Brooklyn NY, U.S. - Founder of Pickwick Records - Was a Vice Chairman of The Songwriters Hall Of Fame.**

**Dan Falley - Died 1-6-2008 - Car accident - He was 55 years old - Guitarist - Worked with The Chevelles and Fyrestorm - Was the owner of Dan's Guitar Shop.**

**Samir Hussein - Died 1-6-2008 - Fell from a sixth floor apartment ( Rap ) He was 34 years old.**

**Wally Willette (Wallace D. Willette) - Died 1-6-2008 ( Rockabilly ) Born 7-2-1929 in Bangor, Maine, U.S. - (He did, "Pink Elephants" and "Eenie Meenie") - Rockabilly Hall Of Fame Inductee.**

**Bill Belew - Died 1-7-2008 in Palm Springs, CA, U.S. - Born in Crocet, Vir., U.S. - He was 77 years old - Fashion designer - Created jumpsuits for Elvis Presley and costumes for Josephine Baker, Ella Fitzgerald and Gloria Estefan.**

**Valdo Delgado - Died 1-7-2008 in Uruguay- Car accident ( Charango ) He was 41 years old - Musician - Born in Chile - Worked with Eduardo Pinto.**

**Ichtys Niger - Died 1-7-2008 - Shot himself ( Metal ) Drummer - Was a member of Murder Rape, Insane Devotion and Evil Wars.**

**Roberto del Fierro Lugo - Died 1-8-2008 in Guadalajara, Mexico - Shot - He was 47 years old - Was a marketing manager for Mexican musician, Jesus "El Flaco".**

**[Clyde Otis](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clyde_Otis) (Clyde Lovern Otis Jr.) - Died 1-8-2008 in Englewood, NJ, U.S. - Born 9-11-1924 in Prentice, MS, U.S. - Songwriter and producer - Worked with Brook Benton ("It's Just A Matter Of Time" and "Endlessly") - Produced Sarah Vaughan, Charlie Rich, Sonny James, Timi Yuro and The Diamonds.**

**Sondra Isaminger - Died 1-8-2008 - Cancer ( R&B - Funk - Soul ) She was 51 years old - Singer - Was a member of Under The Influence.**

**Daniel Hetu - Died 1-8-2008 - Cirrhosis of the liver - Born 12-1-1950 in Montreal, Canada - Pianist and songwriter - (He did, "Je t'attendais") - Was a musical director for Rene Simard.**

**Doc Hunter (William Hunter III) - Died 1-8-2008 in San Diego, CA, U.S. - Natural causes ( Jazz ) Born 7-11-1937 in San Bernardino, CA, U.S. - Pianist - Worked with The South Market Street Jazz Band, The Chicago 6 andBill Allred's Classic Jazz Band - He was the husband of dancer, singer and actress, Nanci Hunter.**

**Charlie Hahn (aka Banjeau Chucque ) (Charles Daniel Hahn II) - Died 1-9-2008 - Lung cancer ( Folk - Bluegrass - Gospel - Jazz - Irish ) Born 10-10-1945 in Auburn, Nebraska, U.S. - Played banjo, tin whistle and bodhran - (He did, "Pigs In A Polka") - Worked with Rarely Heard, The Poultrygeist Band and [The Greatful Stones](http://www.soundclick.com/bands/default.cfm?bandID=108573).**

**[Lew Spence](http://www.cabaretwest.org/d_lewspence.html) - Died 1-9-2008 in Los Angeles, CA, U.S. - Born 6-29-1920 in Cedarhurst, Long Island, NY, U.S. - Composer - (He co-wrote, "So Long My Love" and "Nice 'n Easy") - His songs have been done by Frank Sinatra, Tony Bennett, Bobby Short, Peggy Lee, Nat King Cole, Johnny Mathis, Bing Crosby, Billy Eckstine and Dinah Shore.**

**Dr. Kenneth R. Henderson - Died 1-9-2008 - Born 1-19-1935 in Wheatland, Wyo., U.S. - Played trumpet - Was a member of The Golden Eagle Concert Band.**

**Dr. Roi Kwabena (Roi Ankhkara Kwabena) - Died 1-9-2008 - Born 1956 in Trinidad - Poet, musician, historian and publisher - Worked with Hugh Masekela, Linton Kwesi Johnson, Opai Adisa Palmer.**

**Rod Allen (Rodney Bainbridge) - Died 1-10-2008 in Coventry - Liver cancer ( Rock ) Born 3-31-1944 in Leicester, Leicestershire, England - Singer and bassist - Was a member of The Cliftones who became [The Fortunes](http://www.thefortunes.co.uk/) (They did, "You've Got Your Troubles" and "Here Comes That Rainy Day Feeling").**

**2008 July to December**
**Derek Tatam - Died 2009 - Illness ( Jazz ) He was in his late 60s - Played trumpet - Worked with Alvin Roy, The Chicagoans, The Royal Garden Jazzmen and The Tubby Hickman Quintet.**

**[Mel Galley](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mel_Galley) (Melville Galley) - Died 7-1-2008 in Cannock, Staffordshire, England - Cancer of the oesophagus ( Rock ) Born 3-8-1948 in Cannock, Staffordshire, England - Guitarist, songwriter and singer - Was a member of [Whitesnake](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitesnake) (They did, "Here I Go Again" and "Love Ain't No Stranger"), [Trapeze](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trapeze_%28band%29) (They did, "It's Only A Dream" and "Another Day"), [Phenomena](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenomena_II) and [Finders Keepers](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finders_Keepers_%28band%29) (They did, "Sadie, The Cleaning Lady") - Worked with Cozy Powell ("Formula One").**

**Johnny Schou - Died 7-1-2008 in Fort Collins, Colorado, U.S. - Heroin overdose ( Rock ) He was 22 years old - Bassist and guitarist - Was a member of [Tickle Me Pink](http://www.ticklemepinkrock.com/) (They did, "Typical" and "Madeline").**

**Rodney Tyrone Jennings Jr. - Died 7-1-2008 - Shot - He was 21 years old - Drummer and producer - Formed Rod Productions and Anotha Level Records.**

**Jerry Ritchie - Died 7-1-2008 in Nesbit, MS, U.S. - Cancer ( Gospel ) Singer - Was a member of [Gold City](http://www.goldcityqt.com/) (They did, "I Think I'll Read It Again" and "No Other Word For Grace But Amazing").**

**Russ Sankey (Russell Frederick Sankey) - Died 7-1-2008 - Complications of cancer ( Rock ) Born 4-22-1949 - Guitarist - Was a member of [Reign](http://www.pnwbands.com/reign.html) (They did, "Sea Of Dreams").**

**Tommy Milburn - Died 7-1-2008 - After after falling through a skylight of a restaurant ( Rock ) He was 20 years old - Drummer - Worked with [The SSRIs](http://profile.myspace.com/index.cfm?fuseaction=user.viewprofile&friendid=100770702).**

**[Natasha Shneider](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natasha_Shneider) - Died 7-2-2008 - Cancer ( Rock ) Born 5-22-1956 in Moscow, Russia - Singer, bassist and keyboardist - (She did, "Who's In Control") - Was a member of Walk The Moon and[Eleven](http://www.elevenworld.com/) (They did, "Reach Out" and "All My Friends") - Worked with Queens Of The Stone Age and Chris Cornell.**

**[Paul Varley](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Varley) - Died 7-2-2008 in London England - Pneumonia ( Rock ) Born 5-24-1949 in Preston, Lancashire, England - Drummer - Worked with Purple Haze which became [Little Free Rock](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Free_Rock), Ginger Johnson's African Drums, Streak (They did, "Bang Bang Bullit"), [The Arrows](http://www.geocities.com/arrowmaniax/) (They did, "Touch Too Much" and the original version of, "[I Love Rock N Roll](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Love_Rock_%27N%27_Roll)"), [Darling](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darling_(band)), The Ruffians, Terry Reid and Paul Raymond.**

(They did, "Fruitless Ways" and "Shake").**

**The Marshall Tucker Band** is an American band from [Spartanburg, South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spartanburg,_South_Carolina "Spartanburg, South Carolina"). Noted for incorporating [blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blues "Blues"), [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music"), [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") and [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz") into an eclectic sound, the Marshall Tucker Band helped establish the [Southern rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_rock "Southern rock") genre in the early 1970s.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Marshall_Tucker_Band#cite_note-larkin-1) While the band had reached the height of its commercial success by the end of the decade, it has recorded and performed continuously under various line-ups for 50 years.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Marshall_Tucker_Band#cite_note-larkin-1) Lead vocalist [Doug Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doug_Gray "Doug Gray") remains the only original member still active with the band.

The original line-up of the Marshall Tucker Band, formed in 1972, included [lead guitarist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_guitarist "Lead guitarist"), vocalist and primary songwriter [Toy Caldwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toy_Caldwell "Toy Caldwell") (1947–1993), lead vocalist [Doug Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doug_Gray "Doug Gray") (born 1948), keyboard player, saxophone player and [flautist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flautist "Flautist")[Jerry Eubanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Eubanks "Jerry Eubanks") (born 1950), rhythm guitarist [George McCorkle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_McCorkle "George McCorkle") (1946–2007), drummer Paul Riddle (born 1953) and bassist [Tommy Caldwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Caldwell_(musician) "Tommy Caldwell (musician)") (1949–1980). They signed with [Capricorn Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capricorn_Records "Capricorn Records") and released their first album in 1973, _[The Marshall Tucker Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Marshall\_Tucker\_Band\_(album) "The Marshall Tucker Band (album)")_.

After Tommy Caldwell was killed in a car accident in 1980, he was replaced by bassist Franklin Wilkie. Most of the original band members had left by 1984.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Marshall_Tucker_Band#cite_note-olson-2) The band's current line-up consists of Gray on vocals; keyboard player, saxophonist and flautist Marcus James Henderson; guitarists Chris Hicks, Rick Willis, and Chris Anderson, bassist Ryan Ware and drummer Leroy Wilson.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Marshall_Tucker_Band#cite_note-3)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Marshall_Tucker_Band&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Early history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Marshall_Tucker_Band&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early history")]

The original members (and some later members) of the Marshall Tucker Band had been playing in various line-ups under different band names around the Spartanburg area since the early 1960s. In 1966 members of several such bands merged to form the Toy Factory, named after guitarist Toy Caldwell. The Toy Factory's constantly shifting line-up included, at various times, Caldwell, his younger brother Tommy, Doug Gray, Jerry Eubanks, George McCorkle and Franklin Wilkie. In the late 1960s, four of the band members served in the US military;[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Marshall_Tucker_Band#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Marshall_Tucker_Band#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Marshall_Tucker_Band#cite_note-6) Toy Caldwell served in the Marine Corps and received a Purple Heart after being wounded in [Vietnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Marshall_Tucker_Band#cite_note-7)

By the 1970s, Toy Caldwell and George McCorkle had returned to Spartanburg and the Toy Factory had resumed playing in area clubs.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Marshall_Tucker_Band#cite_note-smith-8)

In 1972 Caldwell and McCorkle once again revamped the band's line-up, eventually settling on Tommy Caldwell on bass/backing vocals, George McCorkle rhythm guitar/banjo, vocalist Doug Gray and Jerry Eubanks, keyboards/flute/tenor sax/backing vocals, while adding Paul Riddle on drums; the new line-up adopted the name "Marshall Tucker Band".

[Wet Willie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wet_Willie "Wet Willie") lead singer [Jimmy Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Hall "Jimmy Hall") told Toy Caldwell to book the band at Grant's Lounge in [Macon, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macon,_Georgia "Macon, Georgia"), which he did. After hearing the band play at Grant's Lounge, Buddy Thornton and [Paul Hornsby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Hornsby "Paul Hornsby") recorded the band's [demo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demo_(music) "Demo (music)") at [Capricorn Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capricorn_Records "Capricorn Records"). [Frank Fenter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Fenter "Frank Fenter") and [Phil Walden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Walden "Phil Walden") signed the Marshall Tucker Band to [Capricorn Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capricorn_Records "Capricorn Records") based on those demos.

Not to be confused with [Buckingham Nicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckingham_Nicks "Buckingham Nicks") or [Lindsey Buckingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsey_Buckingham "Lindsey Buckingham").

**The Buckinghams** are an American [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-2) band from [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"). They formed in 1966 and went on to become one of the top-selling acts of 1967, charting their only five top 40 hits in the U.S. that year. The band dissolved in 1970, but re-formed in 1980 and as of 2026[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Buckinghams&action=edit) they continue to tour throughout the United States.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Buckinghams&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

In 1965 guitarists Carl Giammarese and Nick Fortuna, along with bassist Curtis Bachman, were invited to join a band called the Centuries. Giammarese and Bachman, plus keyboardist Dennis Miccolis, later became members of another band, the Pulsations, whose members included drummer [John Poulos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Poulos "John Poulos") and vocalists George LeGros and [Dennis Tufano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Tufano "Dennis Tufano"). After winning a local battle of the bands competition in late 1965, the Pulsations secured a job as the house band on [WGN-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WGN-TV "WGN-TV")'s variety show called _All-Time Hits_. The show's producers suggested they adopt a name reflective of the [British Invasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Invasion "British Invasion"), which was popular at the time, and the band adopted the name _The Buckinghams_, which was suggested by a security guard named John Opager at the station. The band liked the name because of its similarity to a hometown landmark, [Buckingham Fountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckingham_Fountain "Buckingham Fountain").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-Official-3)

In early 1966, LeGros was forced to leave after he was drafted. Right around the same time, bassist Bachman also left and Fortuna (now playing bass and soon briefly going under the surname of Fortune, after it was misspelled on the record jacket) returned after a stint with Jimmy V. & the Entertainers.

The band then signed their first record contract with local label USA Records and recorded 12 songs that year. Several were released as singles, including "[I'll Go Crazy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'll_Go_Crazy_(James_Brown_song) "I'll Go Crazy (James Brown song)")", a song originally recorded by [James Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Brown "James Brown")&[the Famous Flames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Famous_Flames "The Famous Flames") and [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles")' "[I Call Your Name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Call_Your_Name "I Call Your Name")". However, it was their number one single "[Kind of a Drag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kind_of_a_Drag "Kind of a Drag")" that provided them with national exposure. "Kind of a Drag" was written by Chicago-based songwriter [Jim Holvay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Holvay "Jim Holvay"), who had been performing with a group called The Mob,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-4) and spent two weeks at the top of the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") in February 1967. It sold over one million copies, and was awarded a [gold disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_recording_sales_certification "Music recording sales certification").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-The_Book_of_Golden_Discs-5) The co-producers of "Kind of a Drag" were the band's first personal manager [Carl Bonafede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Bonafede "Carl Bonafede") and big band leader Dan Belloc, owner of the Holiday Ballroom in Chicago. The horns on the song were arranged by Frank Tesinsky and the engineer at the first recording sessions held at [Chess Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess_Records "Chess Records") in Chicago was [Ron Malo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Malo "Ron Malo"). Following this, the band's debut album, also entitled _Kind of a Drag_, was released on USA Records and featured the band's early recordings.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-Nite,_Norm_N._1978_p._58-6)

In late 1966, keyboardist Miccolis was replaced by [Larry Nestor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Nestor "Larry Nestor"), who stayed in the band only a short time and was in turn replaced by [Marty Grebb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marty_Grebb "Marty Grebb") at the close of 1966.

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/The_Buckinghams_in_1967.jpg/250px-The_Buckinghams_in_1967.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Buckinghams_in_1967.jpg)

The Buckinghams featured in May 6, 1967 issue of [KRLA Beat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KRLA_Beat "KRLA Beat")

Around this time the band members were introduced to [James William Guercio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_William_Guercio "James William Guercio"), formerly the bassist and road manager for [Chad & Jeremy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad_&_Jeremy "Chad & Jeremy"), who then signed them to a management contract with Ebbins-Guercio Associates.

The Buckinghams were then courted by several record labels before deciding on promotion specialist Jim Scully, who quickly got them a new contract with [Columbia (CBS) Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-7) And Guercio, who became the group's producer, continued the group's "brass-rock" approach, and the band produced four more Top-20 hits in 1967: "[Don't You Care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_You_Care "Don't You Care")" (No. 6), "[Mercy, Mercy, Mercy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercy,_Mercy,_Mercy "Mercy, Mercy, Mercy")" (No. 5), "[Hey Baby (They're Playing Our Song)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_Baby_(They're_Playing_Our_Song) "Hey Baby (They're Playing Our Song)")" (No. 12) and "[Susan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_(song) "Susan (song)")" (No. 11), three of which were written by [Jim Holvay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Holvay "Jim Holvay") and [Gary Beisbier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Beisbier "Gary Beisbier").

Musical artist

**Ronald Belford****"Bon"****Scott** (9 July 1946– 19 February 1980) was an Australian singer who was the second lead vocalist and lyricist of the [hard rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_rock "Hard rock") band [AC/DC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC/DC "AC/DC") from 1974 until his death in 1980.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-hell_aint-1) In the July 2004 issue of _[Classic Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classic\_Rock\_(magazine) "Classic Rock (magazine)")_, Scott was ranked number one in a list of the "100 Greatest Frontmen of All Time".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-Classic_Rock_2004-2)_[Hit Parader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit\_Parader "Hit Parader")_ ranked Scott as fifth on their 2006 list of the 100 Greatest Heavy Metal Vocalists of all time.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-3)

Born in [Forfar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forfar "Forfar") in [Angus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angus,_Scotland "Angus, Scotland"), Scotland, Scott spent his early years in [Kirriemuir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirriemuir "Kirriemuir"). He moved to Australia with his family in 1952 at the age of six, living in [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne") for four years before settling in the Perth neighbourhood of [Fremantle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fremantle "Fremantle"), [Western Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Australia "Western Australia"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-hell_aint-1) then [Adelaide, South Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide,_South_Australia "Adelaide, South Australia") in his later years. Scott formed his first band, [the Spektors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Spektors "The Spektors"), in 1964 and became the band's drummer and occasional lead vocalist. He performed in several other bands, including [the Valentines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Valentines_(rock_band) "The Valentines (rock band)") and [Fraternity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraternity_(band) "Fraternity (band)"), before replacing original AC/DC lead singer [Dave Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Evans_(singer) "Dave Evans (singer)") in 1974.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-hell_aint-1)

With AC/DC, Scott performed on the band's first seven albums: _[High Voltage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High\_Voltage\_(1975\_album) "High Voltage (1975 album)")_ (1975, Oceania only release), _[T.N.T.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T.N.T.\_(album) "T.N.T. (album)")_ (1975, Oceania only release), _[High Voltage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High\_Voltage\_(1976\_album) "High Voltage (1976 album)")_ (1976, first international release), _[Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirty\_Deeds\_Done\_Dirt\_Cheap "Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap")_ (1976, not released until 1981 in the United States), _[Let There Be Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let\_There\_Be\_Rock "Let There Be Rock")_ (1977), _[Powerage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Powerage "Powerage")_ (1978) and _[Highway to Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highway\_to\_Hell "Highway to Hell")_ (1979). AC/DC's popularity grew throughout the 1970s, initially in Australia, and then internationally. From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

The following is a list of notable performers of [rock music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") and other forms of [popular music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_music "Popular music"), and others directly associated with the music as producers, songwriters or in other closely related roles, who died in the 2010s decade. The list gives their date, cause and location of death, and their age.

Rock music developed from the rock and roll music that emerged during the 1950s, and includes a diverse range of subgenres. The terms "rock and roll" and "rock" each have a variety of definitions, some narrow and some wider. In determining criteria for inclusion, this list uses as its basis reliable sources listing "rock deaths" or "deaths in rock and roll", as well as such sources as the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame").

It was alleged that he became a millionaire as a teenager but sadly died in a religious facility due to a chronic viral infection. Musical artist

**Ronald Belford****"Bon"****Scott** (9 July 1946– 19 February 1980) was an Australian singer who was the second lead vocalist and lyricist of the [hard rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_rock "Hard rock") band [AC/DC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC/DC "AC/DC") from 1974 until his death in 1980.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-hell_aint-1) In the July 2004 issue of _[Classic Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classic\_Rock\_(magazine) "Classic Rock (magazine)")_, Scott was ranked number one in a list of the "100 Greatest Frontmen of All Time".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-Classic_Rock_2004-2)_[Hit Parader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit\_Parader "Hit Parader")_ ranked Scott as fifth on their 2006 list of the 100 Greatest Heavy Metal Vocalists of all time.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-3)

Born in [Forfar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forfar "Forfar") in [Angus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angus,_Scotland "Angus, Scotland"), Scotland, Scott spent his early years in [Kirriemuir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirriemuir "Kirriemuir"). He moved to Australia with his family in 1952 at the age of six, living in [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne") for four years before settling in the Perth neighbourhood of [Fremantle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fremantle "Fremantle"), [Western Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Australia "Western Australia"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-hell_aint-1) then [Adelaide, South Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide,_South_Australia "Adelaide, South Australia") in his later years. Scott formed his first band, [the Spektors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Spektors "The Spektors"), in 1964 and became the band's drummer and occasional lead vocalist. He performed in several other bands, including [the Valentines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Valentines_(rock_band) "The Valentines (rock band)") and [Fraternity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraternity_(band) "Fraternity (band)"), before replacing original AC/DC lead singer [Dave Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Evans_(singer) "Dave Evans (singer)") in 1974.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-hell_aint-1)

With AC/DC, Scott performed on the band's first seven albums: _[High Voltage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High\_Voltage\_(1975\_album) "High Voltage (1975 album)")_ (1975, Oceania only release), _[T.N.T.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T.N.T.\_(album) "T.N.T. (album)")_ (1975, Oceania only release), _[High Voltage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High\_Voltage\_(1976\_album) "High Voltage (1976 album)")_ (1976, first international release), _[Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirty\_Deeds\_Done\_Dirt\_Cheap "Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap")_ (1976, not released until 1981 in the United States), _[Let There Be Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let\_There\_Be\_Rock "Let There Be Rock")_ (1977), _[Powerage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Powerage "Powerage")_ (1978) and _[Highway to Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highway\_to\_Hell "Highway to Hell")_ (1979). AC/DC's popularity grew throughout the 1970s, initially in Australia, and then internationally. Their 1979 album _Highway to Hell_ reached the top 20 in the United States, and was their commercial breakthrough. However, on 19 February 1980, Scott died after a night out in London with former musician and alleged drug dealer Alistair Kinnear. AC/DC briefly considered disbanding, but the group recruited vocalist [Brian Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Johnson "Brian Johnson") of the British [glam rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glam_rock "Glam rock") band [Geordie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geordie_(band) "Geordie (band)"). AC/DC's subsequent album, _[Back in Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back\_in\_Black "Back in Black")_, was released only five months later, and was a tribute to Scott. It is currently the [second-best-selling album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_albums "List of best-selling albums") of all time.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-hell_aint-1)

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bon_Scott&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

### 1946–1964: Early years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bon_Scott&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 1946–1964: Early years")]

Ronald Belford Scott was born on 9 July 1946 at Fyfe Jamieson Maternity Hospital in [Forfar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forfar "Forfar"), Scotland, to Charles Belford "Chick" Scott (1917–1999) and Isabelle Cunningham "Isa" Mitchell (1917–2011). He grew up in [Kirriemuir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirriemuir "Kirriemuir") and was the Scotts' second child.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-hell_aint-1) A third child, another son, was born in 1949.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-hell_aint-1) Chick and Isa ran the family bakery in Kirriemuir's Bank Street.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-4) The family emigrated from Scotland to Australia in 1952.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-5)

The Scotts lived in the Melbourne suburb of [Sunshine, Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunshine,_Victoria "Sunshine, Victoria"), and Scott attended the nearby Sunshine Primary School.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-hell_aint-1) He received the nickname "Bon" shortly after starting school; because there was another Ronald in the class, his classmates played on the phrase "Bonnie Scotland".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-6) A fourth child, a son, was born in 1953.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-hell_aint-1)

In 1956, the family moved to [Fremantle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fremantle "Fremantle"), Western Australia. Scott joined the associated Fremantle Scots [Pipe Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pipe_Band "Pipe Band"), learning the drums.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-hell_aint-1) He attended North Fremantle Primary School and later [John Curtin Senior High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Curtin_College_of_the_Arts "John Curtin College of the Arts") until he dropped out at the age of 15. He subsequently worked as a farmhand and a crayfisherman, and was later a trainee weighing-machine mechanic.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-7) In 1963 he spent a short time in [Fremantle Prison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fremantle_Prison "Fremantle Prison")'s assessment centre and nine months at the Riverbank Juvenile Institution, relating to charges of giving a false name and address to the police, having escaped legal custody, having unlawful [carnal knowledge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnal_knowledge "Carnal knowledge"), and stealing 12 imperial gallons (55 L) of petrol.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-hell_aint-1) He attempted to join the [Australian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Army "Australian Army"), but was rejected and deemed "socially maladjusted".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWalker199439-8)

### 1964–1970: The Spektors and the Valentines

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bon_Scott&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1964–1970: The Spektors and the Valentines")]

Scott's vocals were inspired by his idol, [Little Richard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Richard "Little Richard").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-9) After working as a postman,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-bonscott.com.au-10) bartender[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-bonscott.com.au-10) and truck packer,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-bonscott.com.au-10) Scott started his first band, [the Spektors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Spektors "The Spektors"), in 1964 as drummer and occasional lead singer.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWalker199432-11) In 1966, they merged with another local band, the Winstons, and formed [the Valentines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Valentines_(rock_band) "The Valentines (rock band)"), in which Scott was co-lead singer with [Vince Lovegrove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Lovegrove "Vince Lovegrove").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-bonscott.com.au-10) The Valentines recorded several songs written by [George Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Young_(rock_musician) "George Young (rock musician)") of [the Easybeats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Easybeats "The Easybeats"). "[Every Day I Have to Cry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Every_Day_I_Have_to_Cry_(song) "Every Day I Have to Cry (song)")" (a song originally written and sung by [Arthur Alexander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Alexander "Arthur Alexander")) made the local [record chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_chart "Record chart").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-hell_aint-1) In 1970, after gaining a place on the [National Top 30](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts") with their single "Juliette", The Valentines disbanded due to artistic differences after a much-publicised drug scandal.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-amg-12)

### 1970–1973: Fraternity and the Mount Lofty Rangers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bon_Scott&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1970–1973: Fraternity and the Mount Lofty Rangers")]

Scott relocated to [Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide "Adelaide") in November 1970 after he joined the Sydney-formed [progressive rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_rock "Progressive rock") group [Fraternity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraternity_(band) "Fraternity (band)") on lead vocals.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-13)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-bonscott.com.au-10) They had local chart success with their version of [Blackfeather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackfeather "Blackfeather")'s "[Seasons of Change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seasons_of_Change "Seasons of Change")" (March 1971). Scott had previously played recorder on Blackfeather's version. Fraternity released the [LPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gramophone_record "Gramophone record")_[Livestock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livestock\_(Fraternity\_album) "Livestock (Fraternity album)")_ and _[Flaming Galah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flaming\_Galah "Flaming Galah")_ before touring the UK in 1973, where they changed their name to Fang. During this time they played support slots for [Status Quo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Status_Quo_(band) "Status Quo (band)") and [Geordie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geordie_(band) "Geordie (band)"), whose front man [Brian Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Johnson "Brian Johnson") would eventually succeed Scott as the lead singer of AC/DC after his death.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-hell_aint-1) During this time, on 24 January 1972, Scott married Irene Thornton.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-bonscott_story-14)

In 1973, just after returning to Australia from the tour of the UK, Fraternity went on hiatus. Scott took a day job at the Wallaroo fertiliser plant and began singing with the Mount Lofty Rangers, a loose collective of musicians helmed by [Peter Head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Head "Peter Head") (né Beagley) from [Headband](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headband_(band) "Headband (band)"), who explained, "Headband and Fraternity were in the same management stable and we both split about the same time so the logical thing was to take members from both bands and create a new one... the purpose of the band was for songwriters to relate to each other and experiment with songs, so it was a hotbed of creativity".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-15) Other ex-Fraternity members also played with the band as did [Glenn Shorrock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Shorrock "Glenn Shorrock") pre [Little River Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_River_Band "Little River Band"). During this time, Head also helped Scott with his original compositions.

Vince Lovegrove said, "Bon would go to Peter's home after a day of (literally) shovelling shit, and show him musical ideas he had had during his day's work. Bon's knowledge of the guitar was limited, so Peter began teaching him how to bridge chords and construct a song. One of the songs from these sessions was a ballad called 'Clarissa', about a local Adelaide girl. Another was the country-tinged 'Bin Up in the Hills Too Long', which for me was a sign of things to come with Bon's lyrics; simple, clever, sardonic, tongue-in-cheek..."[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-ReferenceA-16)

In return, Scott recorded vocals for Mount Lofty Rangers songs "Round & Round" and "Carey Gully".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-17) Head released these original recordings in 1996, also teaming up with producer Ted Yanni, another old friend of Scott's, to create an entirely new backing for _[Round & Round & Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter\_Head#Bon\_Scott\_and\_'Round\_and\_Round\_and\_Round'\_EP "Peter Head")_ that more accurately reflected the original intentions Head had. Long out of print, and massively bootlegged, this EP finally got an official digital release in June 2010. Unrecorded original compositions of Scott's, "Been Up in the Hills Too Long" and "Clarissa" have been recorded by Head on his Peter Head & the Mount Lofty Rangers _Lofty_ album, also released in digital format only in 2011.

About 11 pm on 3 May 1974, at the [Old Lion Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Lion_Hotel "Old Lion Hotel") in [North Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Adelaide "North Adelaide"), during a rehearsal with the Mount Lofty Rangers, a very drunk, distressed and belligerent Scott had a raging argument with a member of the band. Scott stormed out of the venue, threw a bottle of [Jack Daniel's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Daniel's "Jack Daniel's") to the ground, then sped off on his [Suzuki GT550](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzuki_GT550 "Suzuki GT550") motorbike.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-ReferenceA-16) Scott suffered serious injuries from the ensuing motorcycle accident, spending three days in a coma and a further 18 days in hospital. During his recovery Vince Lovegrove and his wife gave Scott odd jobs, such as putting up posters and painting the office for their nascent booking/management agency. Shortly afterward, Lovegrove introduced him to AC/DC, who had been on the lookout for a new lead singer.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-amg-12)

"There was a young, dinky little glam band from Sydney that we both loved called AC/DC... Before another AC/DC visit, George Young phoned me and said the band was looking for a new singer. I immediately told him that the best guy for the job was Bon. George responded by saying Bon's accident would not allow him to perform, and that maybe he was too old (9 years older than Angus at the time). Nevertheless, I had a meeting with Malcolm and Angus, and suggested Bon as their new singer. They asked me to bring him out to the Pooraka Hotel that night, and to come backstage after the show. When he watched the band, Bon was impressed, and he immediately wanted to join them, but thought they may be a bit too inexperienced and too young. After the show, backstage, Bon expressed his doubts about them being "able to rock". The two Young brothers told Bon he was "too old to rock". The upshot was that they had a jam session that night in the home of Bon's former mentor, Bruce Howe, and at the end of the session, at dawn, it was obvious that AC/DC had found a new singer. And Bon had found a new band."[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-ReferenceA-16)

Fraternity later reformed and replaced Scott with [Jimmy Barnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Barnes "Jimmy Barnes").

### 1974–1980: AC/DC

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bon_Scott&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 1974–1980: AC/DC")]

Main article: [AC/DC §Bon Scott era (1974–1980)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC/DC#Bon_Scott_era_(1974%E2%80%931980) "AC/DC")

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8d/ACDC-Hughes-long_ago.jpg/250px-ACDC-Hughes-long_ago.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ACDC-Hughes-long_ago.jpg)

Bon Scott (centre), performing with AC/DC at the [Ulster Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulster_Hall "Ulster Hall") in 1979

Scott's wife, Irene Thornton, later wrote, "The first time Bon saw AC/DC was in August 1974. They came through Adelaide with the [Lou Reed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lou_Reed "Lou Reed") and [Stevie Wright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Wright "Stevie Wright") tour, and played their own show at the Pooraka Hotel... The first time I saw AC/DC was at the Pooraka Hotel in September. 'Get up there, Bon,' Vince kept saying. The band didn't have a singer that night; they were playing instrumental versions of old rock 'n' roll standards. The boys ripped through all these classic numbers and then finally, with enough pressure from Vince, Bon climbed onto the stage. I didn't realise that AC/DC had just sacked Dave Evans and they wanted Bon to replace him. Like Bon, the Youngs were Scottish, so there was an instant bond."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-marriage-18)

Scott replaced Dave Evans as the lead singer of AC/DC on 24 October 1974,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-bonscott.com.au-10) when it became obvious the band and Evans were heading in different directions, with Evans having personal clashes with band members and management.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStenning200534-19) Scott's appointment coincided with him working as a chauffeur for the band at the time until an audition promoted him to lead singer.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-20)

With the Young brothers as lead and rhythm guitarists, session drummer [Tony Currenti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Currenti "Tony Currenti") (see [AC/DC line-ups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC/DC_line-ups "AC/DC line-ups")) and George Young as a temporary bassist, AC/DC released _[High Voltage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High\_Voltage\_(1975\_album) "High Voltage (1975 album)")_, their first LP in Australia, in February 1975.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-21) Within a few months Currenti was replaced by [Phil Rudd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Rudd "Phil Rudd") and [Mark Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Evans_(musician) "Mark Evans (musician)") was hired as a permanent bassist, and AC/DC began recording their second album _[T.N.T.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T.N.T.\_(album) "T.N.T. (album)")_, which was released in Australia in December 1975. The first AC/DC album to gain international distribution however was a compilation of tracks from the first two albums, also titled _[High Voltage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High\_Voltage\_(1976\_album) "High Voltage (1976 album)")_, which was released in May 1976. Another studio album, _[Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirty\_Deeds\_Done\_Dirt\_Cheap "Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap")_, was released in September of the same year, but only in Australia; the international version of the album was released in December with a different track listing. The album was not released in the US until March 1981.

In the following years, AC/DC gained further success with their albums _[Let There Be Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let\_There\_Be\_Rock "Let There Be Rock")_ and _[Powerage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Powerage "Powerage")_. The 1978 release of _Powerage_ marked the debut of bassist [Cliff Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cliff_Williams "Cliff Williams") (who had replaced Mark Evans), and with its harder [riffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riffs "Riffs"), followed the blueprint set by _Let There Be Rock_. Only one single was released from _Powerage_—"[Rock 'n' Roll Damnation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_'n'_Roll_Damnation "Rock 'n' Roll Damnation")"—which gave AC/DC their highest chart position at the time, reaching #24. An appearance at [The Apollo, Glasgow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Apollo,_Glasgow "The Apollo, Glasgow"), during the _Powerage_ tour was recorded and released as _[If You Want Blood You've Got It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If\_You\_Want\_Blood\_You've\_Got\_It "If You Want Blood You've Got It")_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-popmatters-22)

The band's sixth album, _[Highway to Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highway\_to\_Hell "Highway to Hell")_, was produced by [Robert John "Mutt" Lange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_John_%22Mutt%22_Lange "Robert John \"Mutt\" Lange") and was released in 1979. It became AC/DC's first LP to break the US top 100, eventually reaching #17, and it propelled AC/DC into the top ranks of hard-rock acts.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-timeline-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-Bonfire-24)

On 9 February 1980, AC/DC appeared on _Aplauso TV_ (Spain) where they played "Beating Around the Bush", "[Girls Got Rhythm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girls_Got_Rhythm "Girls Got Rhythm")", and "[Highway to Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highway_to_Hell_(song) "Highway to Hell (song)")"; this would be Bon Scott's last appearance with AC/DC before his death.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-25)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bon_Scott&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Scott met Irene Thornton, from Adelaide, in 1971 while he was the lead singer for Fraternity. They married in 1972.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-amazon-26) The couple separated after two years of marriage and divorced in 1977, but remained friends until Scott's death.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-bookt-27) After Thornton, Scott had a significant ongoing relationship with Margaret "Silver" Smith, whom he had met in Adelaide in the early 1970s. Scott and Smith broke up in 1977 but were in touch until his death.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-28)

Michael Browning, who managed AC/DC in their early years, stated in his book on managing AC/DC, _Dog Eat Dog_, that he visited Scott in hospital in Melbourne in 1975 after Scott had overdosed on drugs. Browning claimed "Bon was bragging to me the last time he was in that hospital he was visiting two separate girls, both unknown to each other, who were both giving birth to his kids at the same time. So there's at least two of Bon Scott's children out there, or at least two I can vouch for."[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-news-29)

## Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bon_Scott&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Death")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Grave_of_Bon_Scott%2C_Fremantle_Cemetery%2C_Western_Australia_-_20060218.jpg/250px-Grave_of_Bon_Scott%2C_Fremantle_Cemetery%2C_Western_Australia_-_20060218.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Grave_of_Bon_Scott,_Fremantle_Cemetery,_Western_Australia_-_20060218.jpg)

Bon Scott's grave

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/67_Overhill_Road_East_Dulwich.JPG/250px-67_Overhill_Road_East_Dulwich.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:67_Overhill_Road_East_Dulwich.JPG)

67 Overhill Road, East Dulwich, London, the site of Bon Scott's death

Sometime during the late evening of 18 February and early morning of Tuesday, 19 February 1980, Scott passed out and died at the age of 33. He had just visited a London club called [The Music Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KOKO_(music_venue) "KOKO (music venue)"). He was allegedly left to sleep in a [Renault 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_5 "Renault 5") owned by his friend Alistair Kinnear, at 67 Overhill Road in [East Dulwich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Dulwich "East Dulwich").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-30) Later that day, Kinnear found Scott unconscious and alerted the authorities. Scott was taken to [King's College Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's_College_Hospital "King's College Hospital") in [Camberwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camberwell "Camberwell"), where he was pronounced [dead on arrival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_on_arrival "Dead on arrival"). The official report of the coroner concluded that Scott had died of "acute [alcohol poisoning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcohol_poisoning "Alcohol poisoning")" and classified it as "[death by misadventure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_by_misadventure "Death by misadventure")".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-BScottDeath-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-32)

Previously, on 15 February 1980, Scott attended a session where Malcolm and Angus Young were working on the beginnings of two songs that would later be recorded on the _[Back in Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back\_in\_Black "Back in Black")_ album: "Have a Drink on Me" and "Let Me Put My Love into You", with Scott accompanying on drums rather than singing or writing lyrics.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-hell_aint-1) Young has also claimed Scott played drums on "Hells Bells"[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-33) while AC/DC drummer Simon Wright has claimed Angus Young played him a demo of Scott playing drums on "Back in Black".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-34) Days earlier, Scott had gone with [Mick Cocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Cocks "Mick Cocks") to visit their friends the French group [Trust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trust_(French_band) "Trust (French band)") in the Scorpio Sound studio in London, where they recorded the album _[Répression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%A9pression "Répression")_; Scott was working on the English adaptation of texts by [Bernie Bonvoisin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Bonvoisin "Bernie Bonvoisin") for the English version of the album. During this visit, the musicians did a jam session of "[Ride On](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ride_On_(AC/DC_song) "Ride On (AC/DC song)")". This improvised session was Scott's last recording.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-36)

As part of the funeral arrangements, Scott's body was embalmed by [Desmond Henley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desmond_Henley "Desmond Henley");[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-37) it was later cremated, and Scott's ashes were interred by his family at [Fremantle Cemetery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fremantle_Cemetery "Fremantle Cemetery") in Fremantle.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-bonshighway-38) Shortly after Scott's death, the remaining members of AC/DC briefly considered disbanding. However, it was eventually decided that Scott would have wanted them to continue, and with the Scott family's encouragement, the band hired [Brian Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Johnson "Brian Johnson") as their new vocalist.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-maximum-39) Before his death, Scott had praised Johnson and the performer's group [Geordie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geordie_(band) "Geordie (band)") to his friends, comparing the other vocalist to [Little Richard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Richard "Little Richard") and remarking (according to Angus Young) along the lines that Scott had found "a guy that knows what rock and roll is all about".[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-40) In [Jesse Fink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Fink "Jesse Fink")'s 2017 book, _[Bon: The Last Highway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse\_Fink#Bon:\_The\_Last\_Highway\_(2017) "Jesse Fink")_, Fink explores the death of Scott and the surrounding circumstances, presenting alternate theories to the official account. Based on his research, he claims other factors might have played a role in Scott's death; alleging that heroin use could have been involved. He also contends that "the police investigation and the coroner’s inquest were substandard."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-44)

## Lyrics controversy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bon_Scott&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Lyrics controversy")]

Main article: [Back in Black §Lyrics controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back_in_Black#Lyrics_controversy "Back in Black")

Five months after Scott's death, AC/DC finished the work they had begun with Scott; they released _Back in Black_ as a tribute to him, but his name did not appear in the writing credits. The issue of whether Scott's lyrics were used, uncredited, on the album is an enduring topic of debate.

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bon_Scott&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Legacy")]

### Landmarks

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bon_Scott&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Landmarks")]

#### Australia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bon_Scott&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Australia")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/BonScottStatue2_gobeirne.jpg/250px-BonScottStatue2_gobeirne.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:BonScottStatue2_gobeirne.jpg)

Statue of Bon Scott, [Fremantle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fremantle "Fremantle"), Western Australia

Scott's grave site in [Palmyra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palmyra,_Western_Australia "Palmyra, Western Australia") has become a cultural landmark. More than 28 years after his death, the [National Trust of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Trust_of_Australia "National Trust of Australia") declared his grave important enough to be included on the list of classified heritage places.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-bonshighway-38)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-45) It is reportedly the most visited grave in Australia.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-46) On 7 July 2006, to mark his 60th birthday, the Metropolitan Cemeteries Board completed refurbishments on the Bon Scott Grave Area. This consisted of a Bon Scott Arch and Memorial Entrance gate off Carrington Street in the north-west corner of Fremantle Cemetery.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-bonscott_story-14) On 9 July 2006, sixty years to the day from Scott's birth, the bronze plaque was stolen from the site.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-47)

A bronze statue of Scott was unveiled at [Fremantle Fishing Boat Harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fremantle_Fishing_Boat_Harbour "Fremantle Fishing Boat Harbour") in Western Australia on 24 February 2008.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-48) The statue portrays Scott atop a [Marshall amplifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Amplification "Marshall Amplification").

[ACDC Lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACDC_Lane "ACDC Lane") is a street in the [Melbourne central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_central_business_district "Melbourne central business district"). It was renamed on 1 October 2004 as a tribute to AC/DC. The trademark lightning bolt or slash ("/") used to separate the AC and the DC in the band's name contravened the naming policy of the Office of the Registrar of Geographic Names, so the punctuation was omitted on the street sign. Melbourne's Lord Mayor [John So](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_So "John So") launched ACDC Lane with the words, "As the song says, there is a highway to hell, but this is a laneway to heaven. Let us rock". [Bagpipers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Highland_bagpipe "Great Highland bagpipe") then played _[It's a Long Way to the Top (If You Wanna Rock 'n' Roll)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's\_a\_Long\_Way\_to\_the\_Top\_(If\_You\_Wanna\_Rock\_'n'\_Roll) "It's a Long Way to the Top (If You Wanna Rock 'n' Roll)")_. Those were all songs from Bon Scott era. The lane contains a rock 'n' roll nightclub called the Cherry Bar.

#### Scotland

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bon_Scott&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Scotland")]

On 6 May 2006, the town of Kirriemuir in Scotland held a service and unveiled a [Caithness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caithness "Caithness") stone slab commemorating the singer.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-49) A message was read from a long-time friend and fellow member of the Valentines, Vince Lovegrove, in which he said:

> The thing I loved most about Bon Scott, was his almost unique self honesty. What you saw was what you got, he was a real person and as honest as the day is long. To my mind he was the street poet of my generations and of the generations that followed.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-50)

A life-sized bronze statue of Scott was unveiled by former AC/DC bass player Mark Evans in Bellies Brae Car Park in Kirriemuir on 30 April 2016, during the 10th anniversary of the Bonfest music festival. Kirriemuir hosts an annual festival known as "Bonfest" as a tribute to Bon Scott and AC/DC. It was originally held in July on the weekend closest to his birthday but moved to May because of other events in the local area during July. The statue was commissioned by local community group DD8 Music and created by [John McKenna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McKenna_(sculptor) "John McKenna (sculptor)").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-51)

### Posthumous releases

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bon_Scott&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Posthumous releases")]

AC/DC released a [box set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box_set "Box set") entitled _[Bonfire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonfire\_(AC/DC\_album) "Bonfire (AC/DC album)")_ as a tribute to Scott on 18 November 1997. It contains four albums; a [remastered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remaster "Remaster") version of _Back in Black_; a "rarities" album with alternate takes, outtakes, and stray live cuts, _[Volts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volts\_(album) "Volts (album)")_; and two live albums, _[Live from the Atlantic Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live\_from\_the\_Atlantic\_Studios "Live from the Atlantic Studios")_ and _[Let There Be Rock: The Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let\_There\_Be\_Rock:\_The\_Movie "Let There Be Rock: The Movie")_. _Live from the Atlantic Studios_ was recorded on 7 December 1977 at the [Atlantic Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Studios "Atlantic Studios") in New York City. _Let There Be Rock: The Movie_ is a double album which was recorded on 9 December 1979 at the [Pavillon de Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pavillon_de_Paris "Pavillon de Paris") in Paris, and was the soundtrack of the motion picture, _[AC/DC: Let There Be Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC/DC:\_Let\_There\_Be\_Rock "AC/DC: Let There Be Rock")_.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-52)

### Accolades, awards and tributes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bon_Scott&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Accolades, awards and tributes")]

[AC/DC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC/DC "AC/DC")'s seventh studio album _[Back in Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back\_in\_Black "Back in Black")_ was released as a dedication and tribute to Scott. In 2003, Scott was posthumously inducted into the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame") as a member of AC/DC[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-53) with his nephews present to accept the honour in his place.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-54)

In 2003, Scott's final studio album with AC/DC, 1979's _Highway to Hell_ ranked 199 on _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_'s "[The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone's_500_Greatest_Albums_of_All_Time "Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time")".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-55) In 2004, the song "Highway to Hell" that Scott co-wrote with [Malcolm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malcolm_Young "Malcolm Young") and Angus Young ranked 254 on _Rolling Stone_'s [The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_500_Greatest_Songs_of_All_Time "The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-56)

In the July 2004 issue of UK magazine _[Classic Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classic\_Rock\_(magazine) "Classic Rock (magazine)")_, Scott was rated as number one in a list of the "100 Greatest Frontmen", ahead of [Freddie Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Mercury "Freddie Mercury") and [Robert Plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Plant "Robert Plant").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-Classic_Rock_2004-2)[_[page needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing\_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_]

The French rock band Trust wrote their hit song "Ton dernier acte" ("Your Last Act") in memory of Scott in 1980. German hard rock band [Kingdom Come](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_Come_(German_band) "Kingdom Come (German band)") wrote and recorded a song titled "Bon Scott" for their album, _Ain't Crying for the Moon_, as a tribute to the former AC/DC frontman. Romanian hard rock group [Iris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iris_(Romanian_band) "Iris (Romanian band)") recorded the song "Ultimul mic dejun al lui Bon" ("Bon's Last Breakfast") as a tribute to Scott, released on their 1997 album _[Lună plină](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lun%C4%83\_plin%C4%83 "Lună plină")_.

Many artists perform live covers of songs that Scott wrote with AC/DC as a tribute to him. On 19 February 2005, the 25th anniversary of Scott's death, [thrash metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrash_metal "Thrash metal") band [Megadeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megadeth "Megadeth") performed a cover of "Problem Child" as a tribute. Singer and guitarist [Dave Mustaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Mustaine "Dave Mustaine") talked about how much Scott had influenced him. Hard rock band [Guns N' Roses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guns_N'_Roses "Guns N' Roses") frequently perform "[Whole Lotta Rosie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whole_Lotta_Rosie "Whole Lotta Rosie")" in concert and covered it in 1987. AC/DC performed their own song "Ride On" only one time in 2001 as a tribute to Scott.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-57)

### Literature

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bon_Scott&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Literature")]

Scott is the subject of several books including two biographies by [Jesse Fink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Fink "Jesse Fink") - _Bon: The Last Highway_ (2017, updated in 2018 and 2022) and _Bon: Notes from the Highway_ (2024) - and [Clinton Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_Walker "Clinton Walker")'s _Highway to Hell_ (1994 and updated in 2015 and 2023). Fink's books claim that Scott died from a lethal combination of alcohol and heroin, while Walker backs the coroner's finding of alcohol poisoning. The controversial point that he and Walker both agree on is that many of Scott's lyrics were co-opted, uncredited, into _Back in Black_. Other books about Scott include Irene Thornton's memoir _My Bon Scott_ (2014, retitled outside Australia as _Have a Drink on Me_), Mary Renshaw's _Live Wire_ (2015) and Victor Marshall's _Fraternity: Pub Rock Pioneers_ (2021).[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarshall2021-58)

### Film

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bon_Scott&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Film")]

In 2024 it was reported a feature film called _The Kid from Harvest Road_ was being made of Scott's time in Western Australia before he became a musician.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Scott#cite_note-59)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

This is a [dynamic list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Lists#Dynamic_lists "Wikipedia:WikiProject Lists") and may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness. You can help by [editing the page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:EditPage/List_of_2000s_deaths_in_popular_music "Special:EditPage/List of 2000s deaths in popular music") to add missing items, with references to [reliable sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources").

The following is a list of notable performers of [rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll") music or [rock music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music"), and others directly associated with the music as producers, songwriters or in other closely related roles, who have died in the 2000s. The list gives their date, cause and location of death, and their age.

Rock music developed from the rock and roll music that emerged during the 1950s, and includes a diverse range of subgenres. The terms "rock and roll" and "rock" each have a variety of definitions, some narrow and some wider. In determining criteria for inclusion, this list uses as its basis reliable sources listing "rock deaths" or "deaths in rock and roll", as well as such sources as the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame").

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

The following is a list of notable performers of [rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll") music or [rock music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music"), and others directly associated with the music as producers, songwriters or in other closely related roles, who have died in the 1980s. The list gives their date, cause and location of death, and their age.

Rock music developed from the rock and roll music that emerged during the 1950s, and includes a diverse range of subgenres. The terms "rock and roll" and "rock" each have a variety of definitions, some narrow and some wider. In determining criteria for inclusion, this list uses as its basis reliable sources listing "rock deaths" or "deaths in rock and roll", as well as such sources as the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame").

This is a [dynamic list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Lists#Dynamic_lists "Wikipedia:WikiProject Lists") and may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness. You can help by [editing the page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:EditPage/List_of_1980s_deaths_in_popular_music "Special:EditPage/List of 1980s deaths in popular music") to add missing items, with references to [reliable sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources").

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Following is a list of notable performers of rock and roll music or rock music, and others directly associated with the music as producers, songwriters or in other closely related roles, who have died in the 1990s. The list gives their date, cause and location of death, and their age.

Rock music developed from the rock and roll music that emerged during the 1950s, and includes a diverse range of subgenres. The terms "rock and roll" and "rock" each have a variety of definitions, some narrow and some wider. In determining criteria for inclusion, this list uses as its basis reliable sources listing "rock deaths" or "deaths in rock and roll", as well as such sources as the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
