**The Buckinghams** are an American [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-2) band from [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"). They formed in 1966 and went on to become one of the top-selling acts of 1967, charting their only five top 40 hits in the U.S. that year. The band dissolved in 1970, but re-formed in 1980 and as of 2026[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Buckinghams&action=edit) they continue to tour throughout the United States.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Buckinghams&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

In 1965 guitarists Carl Giammarese and Nick Fortuna, along with bassist Curtis Bachman, were invited to join a band called the Centuries. Giammarese and Bachman, plus keyboardist Dennis Miccolis, later became members of another band, the Pulsations, whose members included drummer [John Poulos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Poulos "John Poulos") and vocalists George LeGros and [Dennis Tufano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Tufano "Dennis Tufano"). After winning a local battle of the bands competition in late 1965, the Pulsations secured a job as the house band on [WGN-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WGN-TV "WGN-TV")'s variety show called _All-Time Hits_. The show's producers suggested they adopt a name reflective of the [British Invasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Invasion "British Invasion"), which was popular at the time, and the band adopted the name _The Buckinghams_, which was suggested by a security guard named John Opager at the station. The band liked the name because of its similarity to a hometown landmark, [Buckingham Fountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckingham_Fountain "Buckingham Fountain").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-Official-3)

In early 1966, LeGros was forced to leave after he was drafted. Right around the same time, bassist Bachman also left and Fortuna (now playing bass and soon briefly going under the surname of Fortune, after it was misspelled on the record jacket) returned after a stint with Jimmy V. & the Entertainers.

The band then signed their first record contract with local label USA Records and recorded 12 songs that year. Several were released as singles, including "[I'll Go Crazy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'll_Go_Crazy_(James_Brown_song) "I'll Go Crazy (James Brown song)")", a song originally recorded by [James Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Brown "James Brown")&[the Famous Flames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Famous_Flames "The Famous Flames") and [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles")' "[I Call Your Name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Call_Your_Name "I Call Your Name")". However, it was their number one single "[Kind of a Drag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kind_of_a_Drag "Kind of a Drag")" that provided them with national exposure. "Kind of a Drag" was written by Chicago-based songwriter [Jim Holvay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Holvay "Jim Holvay"), who had been performing with a group called The Mob,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-4) and spent two weeks at the top of the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") in February 1967. It sold over one million copies, and was awarded a [gold disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_recording_sales_certification "Music recording sales certification").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-The_Book_of_Golden_Discs-5) The co-producers of "Kind of a Drag" were the band's first personal manager [Carl Bonafede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Bonafede "Carl Bonafede") and big band leader Dan Belloc, owner of the Holiday Ballroom in Chicago. The horns on the song were arranged by Frank Tesinsky and the engineer at the first recording sessions held at [Chess Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess_Records "Chess Records") in Chicago was [Ron Malo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Malo "Ron Malo"). Following this, the band's debut album, also entitled _Kind of a Drag_, was released on USA Records and featured the band's early recordings.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-Nite,_Norm_N._1978_p._58-6)

In late 1966, keyboardist Miccolis was replaced by [Larry Nestor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Nestor "Larry Nestor"), who stayed in the band only a short time and was in turn replaced by [Marty Grebb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marty_Grebb "Marty Grebb") at the close of 1966.

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/The_Buckinghams_in_1967.jpg/250px-The_Buckinghams_in_1967.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Buckinghams_in_1967.jpg)

The Buckinghams featured in May 6, 1967 issue of [KRLA Beat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KRLA_Beat "KRLA Beat")

Around this time the band members were introduced to [James William Guercio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_William_Guercio "James William Guercio"), formerly the bassist and road manager for [Chad & Jeremy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad_&_Jeremy "Chad & Jeremy"), who then signed them to a management contract with Ebbins-Guercio Associates.

The Buckinghams were then courted by several record labels before deciding on promotion specialist Jim Scully, who quickly got them a new contract with [Columbia (CBS) Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-7) And Guercio, who became the group's producer, continued the group's "brass-rock" approach, and the band produced four more Top-20 hits in 1967: "[Don't You Care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_You_Care "Don't You Care")" (No. 6), "[Mercy, Mercy, Mercy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercy,_Mercy,_Mercy "Mercy, Mercy, Mercy")" (No. 5), "[Hey Baby (They're Playing Our Song)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_Baby_(They're_Playing_Our_Song) "Hey Baby (They're Playing Our Song)")" (No. 12) and "[Susan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_(song) "Susan (song)")" (No. 11), three of which were written by [Jim Holvay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Holvay "Jim Holvay") and [Gary Beisbier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Beisbier "Gary Beisbier").

The same year, the Buckinghams were named by [_Billboard_ magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)") as "The Most Listened to Band in America". But severe differences occurred between the Buckinghams and Guercio, particularly the producer's decision to add a psychedelic section to the song "Susan". The song included a short portion of [Charles Ives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Ives "Charles Ives")' "[Central Park in the Dark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_in_the_Dark "Central Park in the Dark")" and sounded very similar to the Beatles' song "A Day in the Life", with an orchestral crescendo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-8) Many radio stations omitted this section, since it changed the song's tempo and veered radically from the melody.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-9) But the producer had the last word, and the released version kept the psychedelic section intact. The group currently does not include the psychedelic portion in their performances.

By mid-1968, the Buckinghams had parted company with Guercio and Columbia Records assigned staff producer [Jimmy Wisner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Wisner "Jimmy Wisner") to work with the group on their fourth album, _In One Ear and Gone Tomorrow_. The album featured material written by Grebb, Giammarese and Tufano.

Despite the release of a new single, "Back in Love Again", it ended up stalling on the Billboard chart at No. 57, and they were unable to duplicate their 1967 success without Guercio, who went on to take the "brass rock" concept further with [Blood, Sweat & Tears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood,_Sweat_&_Tears "Blood, Sweat & Tears") and [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_(band) "Chicago (band)"). Also, a "Buckinghams Day" in Chicago was cancelled when it was learned that some of the band members were arrested for possession of illegal drugs. It was later determined that marijuana had been found belonging to the band's roadies, and all charges were eventually dropped when the police failed to prove their case. The story of the charges made headlines, but the retraction and resolution of the case as being innocent did not.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-10)

Ultimately, restitution came in the form of recognition as The Buckinghams were inducted into the Iowa Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in September 2019 and the 2022 Inaugural Class of the Illinois Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-11)

By late 1968, Grebb and Fortuna had left and were replaced by keyboardist John Turner and original bassist Bachman, who had gone on to join the band Saturday's Child after leaving the Buckinghams. There were no more hits, though, and the band dissolved in early 1970.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-12)

Columbia released a double compilation record of their two Guercio era albums, _Time and Changes_ and _Portraits_, in 1975 under the title _Made in Chicago_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-Nite,_Norm_N._1978_p._58-6)

After the break-up, Tufano and Giammarese formed the duo Tufano & Giammarese and recorded three albums for [Lou Adler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lou_Adler "Lou Adler")'s record label, Ode Records, forming a touring band in time for their second album. Drummer [John Poulos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Poulos "John Poulos"), who had secured the Ode Records recording contract for the duo, became a manager of several rock bands, including the Boyzz from Illinoizz. Poulos died of drug-related heart failure on March 26, 1980.

## Reformation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Buckinghams&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Reformation")]

Later in 1980, Chicago's WLS radio programming executive John Gehron called Giammarese with an invitation to reunite the Buckinghams for Mayor [Jane Byrne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane_Byrne "Jane Byrne")'s ChicagoFest event in August. Giammarese, Fortuna and Tufano appeared with drummer Tom Osfar and keyboardist John Cammelot on the [Navy Pier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_Pier "Navy Pier") rooftop stage. Marty Grebb declined the opportunity to join them as he was touring with the group [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_(band) "Chicago (band)") at the time.

For the next two years the trio of original members performed at selected concerts in Chicago. When Tufano decided to return to California to resume a career in film voice work in early 1983, Giammarese and Fortuna committed to tour full-time as The Buckinghams.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-13)

The 1983 Buckinghams featured an expanded group that included Giammarese, Fortuna, John Duich (guitar), Tom Taylor (keyboards), Tom Scheckel (drums, percussion) and two female singers: [Laurie Beebe Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurie_Beebe_Lewis "Laurie Beebe Lewis") (vocals, keyboards), who later joined [the Mamas & the Papas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mamas_&_the_Papas "The Mamas & the Papas"),[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-15) and Barbara Unger (keyboards, backing vocals).

In 1984 Duich, Taylor, and Unger were dropped and Giammarese, now handling lead vocal duties, went back to playing guitar as well and Cammelot rejoined on keyboards with Lewis on vocals and supporting keyboards.

The following year the Buckinghams were part of the _Happy Together 85_ Tour, along with [the Turtles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Turtles "The Turtles"), [the Grass Roots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Grass_Roots "The Grass Roots"), and [Gary Lewis and the Playboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Lewis_and_the_Playboys "Gary Lewis and the Playboys"). And that same year they released their comeback album _A Matter of Time_ on Red Label Records[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-16) which included one single promo release "Veronica".

By early 1986, both Lewis and Cammelot left the group and were replaced by Bob Abrams (guitar, vocals) and Bruce Soboroff (keyboards, vocals).

In 1991 [Sony Music Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music_Entertainment "Sony Music Entertainment") (the present-day owner of Columbia Records) released a new greatest hits compilation, _Mercy, Mercy, Mercy: A Collection_. Sony Music has continued to make the Buckinghams' Columbia recordings available, as well as their recordings previously issued by USA Records.

In 1996 the Buckinghams celebrated the band's 30th anniversary with a concert at The Vic Theatre in Chicago. The show was filmed and released as a video entitled "Off Their Rocker" and included DJs [Dick Biondi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Biondi "Dick Biondi") (d. 6.26.23)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-17) and [John Records Landecker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Records_Landecker "John Records Landecker"), still on WGN Radio, as hosts.

## New studio and live recordings (2000–present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Buckinghams&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: New studio and live recordings (2000–present)")]

In 2001 the Buckinghams were part of the _Solid Gold 60s_ Tour along with [Tommy James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_James "Tommy James"), the Turtles, [Gary Puckett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Puckett "Gary Puckett") and the Grass Roots. [PBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PBS "PBS") featured the Buckinghams on _The Sixties Pop Rock Reunion_ in 2004.

In January 2005 the Buckinghams performed at the Twilight on the Prairie Ball for one of President [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush")'s [Inaugural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inauguration_Day "Inauguration Day")[Balls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ball_(dance) "Ball (dance)") in Washington, DC.

In 2007 the Buckinghams signed with national label Fuel Records to release their studio CD _Reaching Back_, which included eight new original songs written by Giammarese and new recordings of five of their top hits. A second CD, _Standing Room Only_ (previously released as _Live and Well_), was also released on the Fuel Label. XM Radio recorded the Buckinghams in concert for their XM Performance Series on the "60s on 6" channel. The Buckinghams' music from yesterday and today remains in regular rotation on classic rock stations in U.S. formats as well as satellite radio and streaming Internet radio stations.

The Buckinghams released their first Christmas album on the BML label, _The Joy of Christmas_, in November 2008. And in December 2008 they debuted the single "Have a Little Faith" on [WGN-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WGN-TV "WGN-TV") in Chicago.

In 2009 the Buckinghams performed at the Bipartisan Illinois Agricultural Ball for the inauguration of President [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama"). The same year, Sony reissued the Buckinghams' first three albums for sale as digital downloads as part of their Legacy Music Series.

On February 9, 2010 the Buckinghams released a DVD/CD [box set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box_set "Box set"), _Up Close_, showing them in concert at the Star Plaza Theatre in [Merrillville, Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merrillville,_Indiana "Merrillville, Indiana").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-It's_About_Music-18)

In May 2010 Abrams and Scheckel left the Buckinghams lineup to be replaced by Dave Zane (guitars, vocals) and Bruce (Rocky) Penn (drums, percussion, backing vocals), who had played with several Chicago-based groups, including the [Cryan' Shames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryan'_Shames "Cryan' Shames") for a number of years. Scheckel went on to join [Paul Revere and the Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Revere_and_the_Raiders "Paul Revere and the Raiders") and stayed until Paul Revere's death, continuing for a time with the renamed band, Paul Revere's Raiders. Scheckel returned to his drum seat in The Buckinghams in April 2023.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-official-19)

On May 20, 2010 Giammarese and Fortuna were featured in the 25th Anniversary Happy Together Tour, joining the Turtles, the Grass Roots, [Micky Dolenz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micky_Dolenz "Micky Dolenz") and [Mark Lindsay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Lindsay "Mark Lindsay") in a 20+-city tour from California to New York, celebrating the silver anniversary of the original Happy Together Tour in 1985. In July 2011 concerts began for the second Happy Together Reunion Tour that included the Buckinghams, the Turtles, the Grass Roots, Mark Lindsay and [the Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Association "The Association").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-20) Later in 2011, it was announced that Carl Giammarese and Nick Fortuna would join the 2012 Happy Together Tour alongside the Turtles, Micky Dolenz, the Grass Roots and Gary Puckett. The popularity of the tour found them rejoining the Happy Together Tour in 2015, 2019, 2021 and 2022 with other artists including The Cowsills, Ron Dante, the Classics IV and the Vogues.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-21)

In 2011 Giammarese completed his solo CD _Journey_, the companion to his future biography, _Reinventing The Buckinghams: My Journey_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-22)

On October 16, 2015 the Buckinghams took part in the filming of _Cornerstones of Rock: American Garage_ which aired multiple times on [WTTW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTTW "WTTW") Chicago. _Cornerstones of Rock_ was created to be a nostalgic celebration of the Chicago-area "garage bands" that rose to national prominence in the 1960s and 1970s. Jim Peterik and [The Ides of March](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ides_of_March_(band) "The Ides of March (band)") served as the house band for the evening, as many original members of these popular bands returned to the concert stage to play their greatest hits. In addition to the Buckinghams, the Cornerstones line-up included the Ides of March, the Cryan' Shames, the [New Colony Six](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Colony_Six "New Colony Six"), the [Shadows of Knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shadows_of_Knight "Shadows of Knight"), [the McCoys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_McCoys "The McCoys") and [the American Breed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_American_Breed "The American Breed"). This special was such a huge success that it spawned a live concert tour which is still continuing. _Cornerstones of Rock: American Garage_ continues to sell out concert venues across the Midwest. The majority of Cornerstones performances are held at the Arcada Theatre (Saint Charles, IL), but as fan demand has grown the tour has branched out to other venues in the Midwest. The 2024 lineup of _Cornerstones of Rock_ contained the Buckinghams, the Cryan’ Shames, the Ides Of March, the Shadows of Knight and the New Colony Six.

The Buckinghams original lead singer Tufano continues to tour as a solo act, and also appears in a [Bobby Darin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Darin "Bobby Darin") show he created, _As Long as I'm Singing_. Former keyboards/vocals/songwriter Grebb played with the Fabulous Rhinestones, Lovecraft (formerly H P Lovecraft), Chicago, [Bonnie Raitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonnie_Raitt "Bonnie Raitt"), the Weight Band, and [Dave Mason](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Mason "Dave Mason"), and has also produced CDs for independent musicians, including [Peach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peach_(singer) "Peach (singer)"). Grebb died on January 1, 2020.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-23)

Giammarese and Fortuna have continued touring with band members Soboroff, Zane, Scheckel and a horn section consisting of Carlo Isabelli (trumpet), Charles Morgan (trombone) and Dan Moffett (tenor saxophone).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Buckinghams#cite_note-official-19) They perform regularly to festival audiences and have played sold-out shows, such as the [Westbury Music Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westbury_Music_Fair "Westbury Music Fair"), the Belfry Theatre, the Egyptian Theatre, the Genesee Theatre, the Arcada Theatre, the Keswick Theatre and others. They remain acts for casino venues and international rock and roll cruises throughout the country and perform the national anthem at home games of baseball teams such as the [Chicago Cubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Cubs "Chicago Cubs") and [White Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_White_Sox "Chicago White Sox").

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

The following is a list of notable performers of [rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll") music or [rock music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music"), and others directly associated with the music as producers, songwriters or in other closely related roles, who have died in the 1980s. The list gives their date, cause and location of death, and their age.

Rock music developed from the rock and roll music that emerged during the 1950s, and includes a diverse range of subgenres. The terms "rock and roll" and "rock" each have a variety of definitions, some narrow and some wider. In determining criteria for inclusion, this list uses as its basis reliable sources listing "rock deaths" or "deaths in rock and roll", as well as such sources as the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame").

This is a [dynamic list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Lists#Dynamic_lists "Wikipedia:WikiProject Lists") and may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness. You can help by [editing the page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:EditPage/List_of_1980s_deaths_in_popular_music "Special:EditPage/List of 1980s deaths in popular music") to add missing items, with references to [reliable sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources").

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Following is a list of notable performers of rock and roll music or rock music, and others directly associated with the music as producers, songwriters or in other closely related roles, who have died in the 1990s. The list gives their date, cause and location of death, and their age.

Rock music developed from the rock and roll music that emerged during the 1950s, and includes a diverse range of subgenres. The terms "rock and roll" and "rock" each have a variety of definitions, some narrow and some wider. In determining criteria for inclusion, this list uses as its basis reliable sources listing "rock deaths" or "deaths in rock and roll", as well as such sources as the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
